High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

sentences.text:
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:182552
Court No. - 73
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 10450 of 2023

Applicant :- Suraj Kumar Sahni
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another

Counsel for Applicant :- Piyush Patel,Pradeep Kumar
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Nalin Kumar Srivastava,J.
1. Crl.
Misc .
Objection Application No.1 of 2023 is allowed.

2. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3.

This application has been moved on behalf of the applicant - Suraj Kumar Sahni seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime No.528 of 2023, under Sections 498-A, 342, 406, 504, 376 IPC,
Police Station Gulriha, District Gorakhpur.

4. It is alleged that the accused applicant was having an affair with the married prosecutrix and when the matter came to the knowledge of her husband and devar, she was sent to the applicant,
who kept her with him for some days and committed rape upon her.
Since report was not lodged at the police station, application u/s 156 (3) Cr.P.C. was moved, which was treated as a complaint case vide order dated 17.9.2022.

The said order was challenged in the revision and following the Suraj Kumar Sahni vs State Of U.P. And Another on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8139699/
1

entities.text: Suraj Kumar Sahni vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: instructions
of the revisional court, fresh order was passed and F.I.R. was lodged in this matter and investigation started, which is going on.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that that applicant is innocent and he has apprehension of arrest in the above-mentioned case, whereas there is no credible evidence against him.
He has been falsely implicated in this matter.
Allegations levelled against the applicant are false.
Investigation is going on into the matter.
It is further submitted that no offence of rape has been committed by the applicant with the prosecutrix.

It is further submitted that the prosecutrix on her own free will, leaving her matrimonial home, came to the house of the applicant with the consent of her in-laws and a compromise had taken place in this respect between both the parties.
In this way, no offence has been committed by the applicant.
It is further submitted that the medical evidence on record does not support the prosecution version.
It is further submitted that the applicant has no criminal history to his credit.
He is cooperating with the investigation and as such he is entitled for anticipatory bail.

6. Per contra, learned A.G.A. vehemently opposing the prayer for anticipatory bail submitted that the applicant was having an affair with the married prosecutrix and when this fact came to the knowledge of her husband, the applicant was called and the prosecutrix was forcibly sent by her in-laws with the applicant, who kept her with him against her wishes and committed rape upon her on many occasions.
Anyhow when the prosecutrix rescued from the clutches of the applicant, the legal proceedings were initiated by her.

It is further submitted that in her statement under section 164 Cr.P.C., the prosecutrix has supported the prosecution version as it is and as such, the applicant is not entitled for anticipatory bail.

7. In the present matter, as it appears from the material placed on record, the prosecutrix, who is a poor married lady, was used as a tool for physical exploitation not only by her in-laws, but by the applicant as well.

In her statement under section 164 Cr.P.C., she has narrated the whole story and the active participation and role of the present applicant is found on the basis of evidence collected by the I.O. during investigation so far.
8.

In Sushila Aggarwal and others vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, (2020) 5 SCC 1, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that while considering an application for grant of anticipatory bail, the court has to consider the nature of the offence, the role of the person, the likelihood of his influencing the course of investigation, or tampering with evidence including intimidating witnesses, likelihood of fleeing justice, such as leaving the country, etc.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal and others vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, (2020) 5 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has further been held that Courts ought to be generally guided by considerations such as the nature and gravity of the offences, the role attributed to the applicant, and the facts of the case, while considering whether to grant anticipatory bail, or refuse it.
Whether to grant or not is a matter of discretion.

9. Hence, considering the settled principles of law regarding anticipatory bail, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusation, role of applicant and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion of the merits of the case, in my view, it is not a fit case to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.
The prayer made in the application is refused.
